# Trailgate

> Camera-trap triage agent. Strands Decider 2B (local, vision, one forward pass) answers three typed questions about every camera-trap frame in one call, and plain Python turns the probabilities into a route: skip (no model, $0), "Nova Lite · Decider confident", "Nova Pro · Decider unsure", or a ranger alert for a person or vehicle. Built for the AWS Builder Center "Agent Experience Hackathon: Strands Decider". Tags: #strands-decider-2b #model-routing. Licence: Apache-2.0.

Repository: https://github.com/ashutosh887/trailgate
Demo (static replay of real Decider answers, Bedrock costs estimated): https://trytrailgate.vercel.app
Dataset: Caltech Camera Traps, https://lila.science/datasets/caltech-camera-traps (CDLA-Permissive)

## The decision handed to Decider

- `present` (noul, yes/no, returns P(true)): "Is there an animal anywhere in this photo, even partly hidden or at the edge?" with explicit true/false criteria.
- `escalate` (noul): "Is there a person or a vehicle in this photo?" with explicit true/false criteria.
- `difficulty` (choice: clear, hard): asked, not used for routing. Measured as a weak signal (AUC 0.67 night vs day; 504 of 600 held-out frames called "hard").
- Policy v2, thresholds frozen on a tuning set of 80 frames from 13 camera locations: alert if P(person or vehicle) >= 0.54 in any frame of the burst; skip if the highest P(animal) in the burst < 0.41 (the burst rule); Nova Lite if P(animal) >= 0.72; otherwise Nova Pro.
- Low-confidence handling: the band between 0.41 and 0.72 is where Decider is unsure, and those frames go to Nova Pro (165 of 600 held-out frames).
- Pattern tag #model-routing: the cheapest tier is no model at all. Without Decider the agent cannot skip, pick a tier, or alert.

## Measured results (held-out: 600 frames, 71 camera locations never used for tuning)

- Empty frames skipped: 150/310 (48.4%); day 51.8%, night infrared 39.0%. 159 of 600 sampled frames (26.5%) reached no model; counted over all 1,079 burst frames, 17.4% reach no model, 46.6% of empty frames are skipped and 23/706 animal frames (3.3%) are skipped.
- Animal frames missed: 9/271 (3.3%). Checked by eye: 1 clearly shows an animal, 4 faint, 4 with nothing visible.
- Vehicles caught: 57/59 (19 held-out frames plus a 40-frame vehicle set).
- 3 of 4 alerts on frames without a `car` label show people that the dataset labels `empty` (no person class); 1 is a true false alert (a deer under a street lamp).
- Calibration: P(animal) >= 0.9 had an animal in 171 of 172 frames; between 0.2 and 0.7 the scores are poorly calibrated.
- Decider latency: p50 472 ms, p90 580 ms per frame over 1,119 calls on an Apple M5 laptop (PyTorch MPS), $0 per call.
- Cost per 10,000 frames, estimated from Bedrock list prices and Nova image token counts (Bedrock quota on the build account was 0, so not measured): Nova Pro on every frame $16.03, Trailgate v2 $5.55 (34.6% of Nova Pro), Nova Lite on every frame $1.20. Lite-only variant of v2: $0.93.
- v1 (route "hard" frames to Nova Pro) skipped 41.9% of empty frames, missed 16/271 animal frames and cost an estimated $10.27. v2 without the burst rule missed 23/271; with it, 9/271.

## Key files

- `patterns/presence_router/`: the reusable decision pattern. `questions.py` (typed questions), `router.py` (framework-free routing, confidence band, burst rule), `handler.py` (Strands `InterventionHandler`: `Deny` skips, `Transform` sets the model tier, fails open), `tune_questions.py` (wording table and skip threshold from your own labelled images), `README.md` (drop-in and threshold guide).
- `trailgate/pipeline.py`: frame check, burst-aware routing, Bedrock calls by tier. `trailgate/bedrock.py`: Nova Converse calls, prices, token estimates. `trailgate/agent.py`: Strands agent with `list_frames`, `archive_empty`, `label_species`, `alert_ranger`, `daily_digest`. `trailgate/server.py` + `trailgate/web/`: ranger console.
- `examples/parcel_photos.py`: the same pattern in a delivery-photo agent.
- `results/metrics.md`: every table. `results/decider_answers.jsonl`: every raw Decider answer. `results/missed.md`: missed-animal gallery. `results/label_audit.csv`: frames checked by eye. `results/thresholds.json`: frozen thresholds and the rule behind each.

## Limits

- v2's threshold values were set on the tuning set, but the v2 policy form (confidence band, burst rule) was chosen after seeing v1's held-out failures, so v2's held-out numbers are a second look at the same frames.
- The Strands agent routes per frame (the ablation policy); the burst rule and published numbers come from the `python -m trailgate run` pipeline.

- Zero-shot vision; thresholds hold for these cameras and need checking on new ones (AUC 0.954 on tuning, 0.900 on held-out).
- Night infrared is weaker (39.0% of empty night frames skipped against 51.8% by day).
- Bedrock costs and Nova species accuracy are not yet measured; `scripts/run_nova_baseline.py` measures them on an account with Nova quota.
- Small sets: 0 errors on a subset means none on these frames, not solved.
